head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Switch the pinned ROCm CI legs from 10.1 to 10.2

Moves the presubmit, continuous and nightly ROCm legs to the ROCm 10.2 GA
images. The rocm10 plugin wheel namespace and the therock-latest legs in the
nightly workflow are unchanged.

Also passes --xla_gpu_blas_max_algorithms=8 to the ROCm tests, as XLA's own
ROCm CI already does (build_tools/rocm/run_xla_ci_build.sh in openxla/xla):
to the Bazel tests in ci/run_bazel_test_rocm_rbe.sh, and to the pytest runs
through ci/utilities/rocm_test_env.sh. Since ROCm 10.2, hipBLASLt returns
many more algorithms for complex64 GEMMs on gfx950 (tuned CGEMM library,
ROCm/rocm-libraries#12722). XLA profiles every candidate while compiling,
which makes //tests:linalg_test_gpu time out on the 10.2 legs. The Bazel
script also runs the JAX leg of openxla/xla's ROCm CI, so this covers that
job too.

display_title: Avoid per-device list allocations in `colocated_cpu_devices`.

head_commit.message:
Avoid per-device list allocations in `colocated_cpu_devices`.

Matching accelerator devices to their colocated CPU devices currently groups
CPU devices into a list per colocation ID even though every valid ID maps to
at most one CPU device. Using a flat dictionary eliminates hundreds of
thousands of single-element list allocations on large meshes and cuts lookup
time by more than half.

`_colocated_cpu_devices_cached` now builds a flat `dict` keyed by
`colocation_id` with a separate `ambiguous_colocation_ids` set, preserving all
existing missing-device and ambiguous-device error messages as well as
`_colocated_cpu_devices_cached_fallback_to_cpu_backend`.

head_commit.message:
Host-side `MaskInfo` preprocessing (`_process_mask`) in JAX Pallas SplashAttention currently slices and materializes every `(q_block, kv_block)` tile via `np.ndindex` and iterates in Python over all blocks in `_get_mask_info_for_shard` and `_shrink_mask_info` / `_shrink_mask_info_dkv`. For long-context masks (8k-131k tokens), this takes tens of seconds on CPU during tracing.

This mirrors the equivalent optimization recently merged in Tokamax (https://github.com/openxla/tokamax/pull/1986).

This change:
- Adds `_classify_mask_blocks` (and `_q_block_stats`) to classify `FullMask`, C-contiguous `NumpyMask`, `CausalMask`, `LocalMask`, `ChunkedCausalMask`, `LogicalOr`, and `LogicalAnd` blocks analytically (`0` = empty, `1` = partial, `2` = full, `-1` = unresolved fallback to per-block slicing).
- Skips `_HashableNDArray` deduplication of partial blocks when `mask_function is not None`, as `MaskInfo` discards `partial_mask_blocks` and `mask_next` when the mask is computed inside the kernel.
- Adds a fast path in `_process_mask` when all heads share the same `Mask` object reference (`head_mask is first_mask`).
- Vectorizes `_get_mask_info_for_shard` using `np.flatnonzero` and `np.searchsorted` for both `is_dkv=False` and `is_dkv=True`.
- Vectorizes `_shrink_mask_info` and `_shrink_mask_info_dkv` across all head shards simultaneously using `np.nonzero` and `np.cumsum`, removing `_slice_mask_info`.
- Adds parameterized unit tests in `tpu_splash_attention_mask_test.py` verifying equivalence between lazy and dense `MultiHeadMask` instances across square and non-square mask/block shapes (`(16, 16)`, `(16, 32)`, `(32, 16)` with block shapes `(4, 4)`, `(4, 8)`, `(8, 4)`), heterogeneous multi-head masks, sharded grids, `is_dkv=True/False`, and non-contiguous `q_sequence` configurations.

display_title: Add fast path for jnp.asarray on arrays

head_commit.message:
Limit jnp.asarray fast path to ArrayImpl

`jax.Array` also matches non-ArrayImpl subclasses such as EArray,
PRNGKeyArray, and UnreducedArray, as well as out-of-tree subclasses that
may customize conversion via `__jax_array__`. Returning those unchanged
skips the normal conversion path, which can change behavior in corner
cases (e.g. `jnp.array` on an Array subclass that defines
`__jax_array__` fails instead of unwrapping it).

Restrict the fast path to ArrayImpl, which covers the eager execution
path being optimized. The explicit Tracer exclusion is no longer needed
because tracers are not ArrayImpl instances. Add a regression test using
an Array subclass that defines `__jax_array__`.

display_title: Ignore compiler_options on nested jit instead of raising during staging.

head_commit.message:
Ignore compiler_options on nested jit instead of raising during staging.

Previously, `pjit_staging_rule` raised `ValueError` whenever a jitted function with `compiler_options` was traced inside a `DynamicJaxprTrace`. That rejected nested `jax.jit` calls as well as top-level transforms that stage a jaxpr without an outer `jit` (such as `jax.linearize` and `jax.make_jaxpr`), breaking library functions that set default `compiler_options` when callers compose them with other transforms:

```python
@jax.jit(compiler_options={"optimization_level": jax.CompilerEffortLevel.O3})
def step(x):
  return jnp.sum(x ** 2)

# Previously raised ValueError during staging:
jax.jit(jax.grad(step))(x)  # now runs; outer jit compiles, inner options logged
y, f_lin = jax.linearize(step, x)  # now runs; top-level primal & tangent keep options
```

Remove the error in `pjit_staging_rule`, skip `Inline.JAX_EARLY` staging-time inlining when `compiler_options_kvs` is non-empty so top-level transforms preserve the options on staged equations, and log ignored nested `compiler_options` during `_pjit_lowering` at `WARNING` when `jax_log_compiles` is enabled and `DEBUG` otherwise. Also restrict the `inlineable` MLIR frontend attribute in `_pjit_lowering` to `Inline.XLA_EARLY` and `Inline.XLA_LATE` so un-inlined `Inline.JAX_EARLY` calls never emit an invalid `inlineable = "jax_early"` attribute.

display_title: Ignore compiler_options on nested jit instead of raising during staging.

head_commit.message:
Ignore compiler_options on nested jit instead of raising during staging.

Previously, `pjit_staging_rule` raised `ValueError` whenever a jitted function with `compiler_options` was traced inside a `DynamicJaxprTrace`. That rejected nested `jax.jit` calls as well as top-level transforms that stage a jaxpr without an outer `jit` (such as `jax.linearize` and `jax.make_jaxpr`), breaking library functions that set default `compiler_options` when callers compose them with other transforms:

```python
@jax.jit(compiler_options={"optimization_level": jax.CompilerEffortLevel.O3})
def step(x):
  return jnp.sum(x ** 2)

# Previously raised ValueError during staging:
jax.jit(jax.grad(step))(x)  # now runs; outer jit compiles, inner options logged
y, f_lin = jax.linearize(step, x)  # now runs; top-level primal & tangent keep options
```

Remove the error in `pjit_staging_rule`, skip `Inline.JAX_EARLY` staging-time inlining when `compiler_options_kvs` is non-empty so top-level transforms preserve the options on staged equations, and log ignored nested `compiler_options` during `_pjit_lowering` at `WARNING` when `jax_log_compiles` is enabled and `DEBUG` otherwise. Also restrict the `inlineable` MLIR frontend attribute in `_pjit_lowering` to `Inline.XLA_EARLY` and `Inline.XLA_LATE` so un-inlined `Inline.JAX_EARLY` calls never emit an invalid `inlineable = "jax_early"` attribute.

display_title: Avoid redundant PRNG work in `jax.random.gumbel` (`mode="highest"`).

head_commit.message:
Avoid redundant PRNG work in `jax.random.gumbel` (`mode="highest"`).

In `float32` `mode="highest"`, the `threefry2x32` PRNG work in `_gumbel` was duplicated since `threefry2x32` already outputs two `uint32` words per hash, but `_random_bits(..., shape=(2,) + shape)` collapsed each pair into one word and ran twice as many hashes.

Fix this by drawing `(hi, lo)` directly as two `*shape` streams via `prng.random_bits(..., num_streams=2)` and hoisting `-jnp.log` out of `jnp.where` to make it easier for XLA to fuse ops while avoiding duplicate PRNG work.

Also, gate the `num_streams=2` path to multi-stream PRNGs (`num_streams >= 2`, i.e., `threefry2x32`, `threefry4x32`, `philox`), and update legacy `threefry2x32.threefry_raw_bits` (`threefry_partitionable=False`) to use a single `(2, *shape)` pass so legacy `gumbel` streams stay bitwise identical and other `num_streams=2` callers avoid a split plus two passes.

head_commit.message:
Avoid redundant PRNG work in `jax.random.gumbel` (`mode="highest"`).

In `float32` `mode="highest"`, the `threefry2x32` PRNG work in `_gumbel` was duplicated since `threefry2x32` already outputs two `uint32` words per hash, but `_random_bits(..., shape=(2,) + shape)` collapsed each pair into one word and ran twice as many hashes.

Fix this by drawing `(hi, lo)` directly as two `*shape` streams via `prng.random_bits(..., num_streams=2)` and hoisting `-jnp.log` out of `jnp.where` to make it easier for XLA to fuse ops while avoiding duplicate PRNG work.

Also, gate the `num_streams=2` path to multi-stream PRNGs (`num_streams >= 2`, i.e., `threefry2x32`, `threefry4x32`, `philox`), and update legacy `threefry2x32.threefry_raw_bits` (`threefry_partitionable=False`) to use a single `(2, *shape)` pass so legacy `gumbel` streams stay bitwise identical and other `num_streams=2` callers avoid a split plus two passes.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Strip device assignment in CPU cache keys

head_commit.message:
Strip device assignment in CPU cache keys

`cache_key.get` currently strips `device_assignment` from serialized `CompileOptions` only on GPU. In multi-process CPU jobs, process-local `jit` calls carry each worker's global device ID in `device_assignment` (`[[0]]` on process 0 vs. `[[2048]]` on process 1). Since XLA:CPU compilation does not depend on `device_assignment`, non-zero processes miss persistent cache entries written by process 0 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So let's strip `device_assignment` when hashing `CompileOptions` on CPU as well, matching GPU.

display_title: Avoid per-device list allocations in `colocated_cpu_devices`.

head_commit.message:
Avoid per-device list allocations in `colocated_cpu_devices`.

Matching accelerator devices to their colocated CPU devices currently groups
CPU devices into a list per colocation ID even though every valid ID maps to
at most one CPU device. Using a flat dictionary eliminates hundreds of
thousands of single-element list allocations on large meshes and cuts lookup
time by more than half.

`_colocated_cpu_devices_cached` now builds a flat `dict` keyed by
`colocation_id` with a separate `ambiguous_colocation_ids` set, preserving all
existing missing-device and ambiguous-device error messages as well as
`_colocated_cpu_devices_cached_fallback_to_cpu_backend`.

display_title: Fix reverse mode through Krylov solvers in custom_root

head_commit.message:
Fix reverse mode through Krylov solvers in custom_root

cg, gmres and bicgstab closed their solve functions over values
computed from `b` (the default x0, and gmres's tolerances). That made
`b` a non-linear input of custom_linear_solve, so its transpose rule
raised NotImplementedError whenever the solve was transposed, e.g. as
the tangent_solve of custom_root or inside a custom_jvp rule.

Compute these values inside the solves from their own right-hand side.
gmres's transposed solve now sets its tolerance from the cotangent's
norm, as cg and bicgstab already did.

Fixes #33872, fixes #5309.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Avoid per-device list allocations in `colocated_cpu_devices`.

head_commit.message:
Avoid per-device list allocations in `colocated_cpu_devices`.

Matching accelerator devices to their colocated CPU devices currently groups
CPU devices into a list per colocation ID even though every valid ID maps to
at most one CPU device. Using a flat dictionary eliminates hundreds of
thousands of single-element list allocations on large meshes and cuts lookup
time by more than half.

`_colocated_cpu_devices_cached` now builds a flat `dict` keyed by
`colocation_id` with a separate `ambiguous_colocation_ids` set, preserving all
existing missing-device and ambiguous-device error messages as well as
`_colocated_cpu_devices_cached_fallback_to_cpu_backend`.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Select `.blockN` scale qualifiers for `tcgen05.mma` by architecture.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Select `.blockN` scale qualifiers for `tcgen05.mma` by architecture.

For 4-bit block-scaled `tcgen05.mma`, the `.block16` / `.block32` qualifiers were only used when K=96 instructions were issued, and `.scale_vec::2X` / `::4X` otherwise. The two are aliases for the default instruction K, and `.blockN` is additionally valid for larger K. Which one to emit is therefore a property of the target, not of the instruction sizes: keep `.scale_vec::NX` on sm_100, where the assembler rejects `.blockN`, and use `.blockN` on sm_103 and later.

This removes the dependency of the qualifier on the K decomposition, in preparation for supporting more instruction K sizes.
